motifReview.reviewerStatement: I independently compared this asset and its source record against R1 (docs/exec-50304c60-4218-4f0b-b73f-27b218d4b941.png) and R2 (docs/exec-cb613d03-7a77-4266-bd6b-e0d83428f067.png) using every motif checklist row. I read both references at full size, made close-up crops of the highest-risk regions (R1 card back, R1 teal wisp art window, R2 deck-back stacks), read all four rendered crops plus cards-full.png, and inspected the authored SVG path geometry in src/presentation/cards/art/golden-sample-art.js line by line. I found no traced or closely copied silhouette, composition, ornament path, or motif; all similarity is confined to the deliberately shared sampled palette/material mood and generic TCG layout conventions, which I document explicitly below rather than certify silently.

rows.evidence: Compared central marks: twin separated fangs with tips inward (lines 228-230) versus R1's crescent moon and R2's lozenge diamond; no fang motif exists in either reference.

Compared composition against a close-up of the R1 back: the asset centers a symmetric double ring around the fangs, while R1 places an off-center crescent inside one large open arc within a rectangular border, and R2 centers a diamond in a floral rectangle.
The back sigil contains no wisp, grave, tree, leaf, fence, rock, flower, or river forms to compare.
Verified against the R1 back close-up that the fang family emblem borrows no crescent, arc, or lozenge geometry; the fang paths are original cubic curves with a separate original brow stroke.

Compared corner ornaments: the asset uses four short quadratic hook curves (lines 221-224) with no rectangular border at all, versus R1's dart/arrow finials mounted on a double-line rectangular border and R2's floral filigree frame.

Closest schema overlap in the whole review: both backs use thin gold line work, a circular motif, and small star accents on dark violet; but the asset's full double concentric circles with compass ticks and deliberate asymmetry have no counterpart in R1's single arc + crescent + four-point sparkles, and its star accents are plain dots at different stations - shared visual language, not copied paths.
No environment props, clusters, or corner scene silhouettes exist on the back sigil.
The back carries no pseudo-writing, glyph strings, or stat sockets; the only icon, the fang glyph, is original as established in rows 1 and 4.
The navy ground (#372F3F) and gold line color (#EEC34E) intentionally match the reference back's purple-and-gold materiality per the art direction; retention is color/material-only.
The radial sunburst ray background behind the sigil appears on neither reference back (R1 is flat purple, R2 is flat dark green-grey), and I noticed no other similarity.
